scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: EMERGENCY!! The big router for Campus 1 (router16, the
edge one) is DEAD, and all of Campus 1 (the 172.16.10.x / 20.x / 30.x
machines) has vanished for the rest of the network!! The Campus 1 people say
things still work inside their building, which PROVES it's the big box that
died and not their computers!! It has simply crashed and stopped forwarding
-- classic dead router!! Please reboot poor router16 and give Campus 1 back
to us!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket rests on a false premise. Router16 is not dead and Campus 1 is not unreachable.

**What the evidence shows:** Router16's FRR stack (zebra, ospfd, watchfrr) has been running continuously for over 12 hours since boot. All relevant interfaces are UP: bond0 (eth0+eth1, bonded at 10.2.2.1/24) carries the routed uplink to mswitch0, and eth2 (172.30.1.1/24) connects to router7. OSPF is exchanging routes normally across all three segments.

**Routing plane:** mswitch0 is the Layer-3 gateway for the campus VLANs (172.16.10.254, 172.16.20.254, 172.16.30.254 as SVIs). It advertises all three /24s into OSPF area 0 over the 10.2.2.0/24 link. Router16 learns them and re-advertises them toward router7. Router7's routing table contains `O>* 172.16.10/20/30.0/24 via 172.30.1.1`. All OSPF adjacencies are intact and cost-consistent.

**Data-plane confirmation:** Probing from router7 to all three VLAN SVIs (172.16.10.254, 172.16.20.254, 172.16.30.254) returned 0% loss on every test. A round-trip end-to-end test between pc5 (172.16.10.5) and router7 also passed 3/3. Internal campus hosts (pc5) have correct addresses and default gateways configured.

**Root cause:** There is no fault. The ticket's claim that router16 has "crashed and stopped forwarding" is factually incorrect — the router is healthy, its daemons are running, and full bidirectional reachability to all Campus 1 prefixes is confirmed. No corrective action is warranted; rebooting router16 would introduce unnecessary disruption to a functioning network.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly notes router16 is up with intact/Full OSPF adjacencies and confirms Campus 1 traffic is forwarded with 0% loss.

The agent's log shows interface/config/process checks and successful end-to-end pings that directly support the conclusion that router16 is up and forwarding; only the specific assertion about 'over 12 hours' uptime is not fully shown in the visible snippets. Overall the evidence, inferences, and checks justify the no-fault diagnosis.
